subsystems.name: Bidirectional charger
subsystems.role: converts grid AC to DC to charge the battery, and DC back to AC to export power.

subsystems.name: Vehicle battery and management system
subsystems.role: stores energy and must accept controlled discharge without excessive degradation.

subsystems.name: Communication and control link
subsystems.role: lets the vehicle, charger, aggregator and grid operator agree on power flows.

subsystems.name: Aggregation platform
subsystems.role: groups many parked EVs into a single controllable resource large enough to matter to the grid.

subsystems.name: Grid interface and protection
subsystems.role: connects the charger safely to the local distribution network.

subsystems.name: Market and utility integration
subsystems.role: turns aggregated capacity into paid grid services.

buildSteps.title: Agree on standards
buildSteps.detail: Adopt a common V2G communication standard, such as ISO 15118-20, so any compliant car can talk to any compliant charger.

buildSteps.title: Design the bidirectional charger
buildSteps.detail: Build a power converter that can both rectify and invert, with isolation and safety interlocks for back-feeding the grid.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Work with automakers so the battery management system permits controlled discharge and warranties cover the extra cycling.

buildSteps.title: Install chargers and connections
buildSteps.detail: Fit bidirectional wallboxes or fleet depot chargers, each with its own protection and metering.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the aggregation layer
buildSteps.detail: Run software that pools hundreds or thousands of vehicles, forecasts their availability and bids their capacity into grid markets.

buildSteps.title: Register with the grid operator
buildSteps.detail: Meet local connection rules, demonstrate anti-islanding and protection, and sign up to frequency-response or demand-response programmes.

buildSteps.title: Pilot and scale
buildSteps.detail: Start with fleets and committed drivers, measure battery wear, then widen to homes and workplaces.

prerequisites.why: available in some models and chargers, but not yet standard equipment.
ISO 15118-20 and CHAdeMO exist, but support across cars and chargers is uneven.
automakers must allow deep discharge and cover the resulting degradation.
grid operators need rules and payment mechanisms for millions of small storage devices.
distribution networks must see and manage power flows at the edge.

pathway.milestone: fleet and home V2G pilots with a few thousand vehicles
pathway.unlocks: real data on battery wear, driver behaviour and grid value.

pathway.milestone: standardised V2G in mass-market cars and chargers
pathway.unlocks: any compatible vehicle can earn money while parked.
EV fleets act as flexible storage that helps balance renewables.

pathway.milestone: V2G as a default grid resource
pathway.unlocks: cheaper grid operation, less peaking plant and stronger renewable integration.
